exposure: type of provider who managed the labor (physician vs. midwife)
cohort: Women admitted for labor and birth in a multihospital regional health system on the Colorado Front Range from January 1, 2018 to January 31, 2020 (N = 10,473).
finding: Racial and ethnic disparities in cesarean birth rates persisted, with several minority groups experiencing significantly higher odds of cesarean birth compared to non-Hispanic White women.
mod_finding: Cesarean birth was more likely when a physician managed the labor course compared with a midwife, for both nulliparous and multiparous women.
